notes.title: My biggest pleasant surprise of 2025 so far has been the free prequel to one of my favorite indie RPGs, made with FromSoft's 25-year-old game making toolset
notes.content: 2023's Lunacid is one of my favorite indies, dungeon crawlers, and just games, period of the last few years. It's a first person RPG taking after FromSoftware's King's Field series, set in an unforgettable subterranean world festooned with secrets. Creator Kira LLC has just released their next project, a follow-up to Lunacid, but there are more than a few twists to it... Read more.

notes.title: Lunacid: Tears of Moon Release
notes.content:
Hello!

Lunacid: Tears of the Moon is now available for free on Steam. It’s a Lunacid spin-off made with the Sword of Moonlight — a toolkit from 2000 used to create King’s Field like games that was released by FROMSOFT. After all, a lot of inspiration for the original Lunacid stems from my deep appreciation of Shadow Tower and King’s Field games. 

[previewyoutube=c_Wf55uc5Vs;full][/previewyoutube]

Tears of the Moon is also a dark fantasy dungeon crawler — full of daunting foes, spells and weapons to obtain and, of course, secrets to discover. The game is very much worth trying out, if you never got to experience the KF series, or feel nostalgic about games of that era.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3506110/Lunacid__Tears_of_the_Moon/ ]https://store.steampowered.com/app/3506110/Lunacid__Tears_of_the_Moon/ [/url]

Naturally, a tool straight from the year 2000 is bound to have a fair share of limitations. However, I very much enjoyed challenging myself to be more creative within these constraints. And I hope, that you could appreciate both this passion and FROMSOFT’s legacy in Lunacid: Tears of the Moon.

Thank you for your support.
Moonlight watch thee.

notes.title: New Languages Added + Steam Winter Sale
notes.content:
Hello!

The localization update is finally here — now the blessings of the Moon can reach you in [b]10 new languages.[/b]

[previewyoutube=Jb05aJsLGIE;full][/previewyoutube]

It definitely took me longer than anticipated — but in return I'm pretty sure the game doesn't mix up Royal and Royalty in other languages. I hope that if English isn’t your native language, [b]these translations will show you the small details you might’ve otherwise missed.[/b]  You can now venture into the Great Well with the following languages on hand:
[list]
[*] Brazilian Portuguese    
[*] Chinese 
[*] Chinese traditional
[*] German 
[*] Korean  
[*] Polish 
[*] Russian  
[*] Spanish   
[*] Spanish LATAM  
[*] Japanese  
[*] Nyan
[/list]
And if your language is not on the list — let me know in the comments. I am open to adding even more popular languages. Also, if you find any localization issues, definitely point them out. So they could be fixed and we would have the best translations possible. 


And, wow, it’s been [b]more than two years since Lunacid launched into Early Access.[/b] It honestly feels like a lucid dream itself — to have come such a long way and [b]to have so many of you enjoy the game. Thank you. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34910757/51b23d9dc2c4e7294661a75804abaeb8e07d9eef.jpg[/img]

[b]I wish that the upcoming year 2025 would be kind to you and your close ones.[/b] And, hey, if you like Lunacid, you might wanna keep an eye on its updates. Maybe follow the game on Steam, if you’d like. Because [b]there is a big announcement waiting for you in 2025.[/b]

The story of Lunacid isn’t quite over just yet.

[i]Moonlight watch thee.[/i]

notes.title: Steam Trading Cards!
notes.content:
Hello!

Thanks to the guiding Moonlight, our prowess and a certain amount of luck — [b]Steam Trading cards for Lunacid are finally available.[/b]

The idea with these was to tie each of the characters to a certain [b]Major Arcana card[/b], but the [i]choices here aren’t exactly ‘canon’[/i]. So it’s best to treat them for what they are — a cool art piece expanding the game. Speaking of! [b]Definitely check out the full versions of the cards[/b], because the small portrait is just a preview.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41193816/88a3cfb2b2261a8ad718c54b4cf183e27f5eef39.png[/img]

Of course, Trading cards also mean [b]profile backgrounds and emojis.[/b] We won’t spoil the surprise here, but [b]the backgrounds were drawn exclusively for Trading Cards[/b] by the same artist as the cards themselves, and [b]the emojis are done by Akuma Kira.[/b]

In other news, [b]the localization update is also coming soon[/b], as promised. Hopefully, this will give some of you extra motivation to revisit the game, if English isn’t your native language. 

The story of Lunacid isn’t quite over just yet.

notes.content: Dark and dingy fantasy dungeon crawler Lunacid has adorned its halls just in time for Halloween, and as a fantasy-loving Halloween fanatic, this is great news for me. Even though the game is already brimming with ghosts and ghouls, KIRA LLC has cut no corners in bringing even more decor to Wing's Rest to help every player celebrate the season, and anyone who feels the same about pumpkins and thematic lighting will probably be just as excited as I am... notes.title: Halloween Update!
notes.content:
Hello!

[b]October is already here[/b], and you know what this means — all manners of scares and seasonal decorations crop up all over the place. You might be surprised, but [b]the denizens of the Wing’s Rest are no exception to this![/b]

[h2]Halloween in Lunacid[/h2]
Wing’s Rest is now adorned with [b]lots of jack-o-lanterns[/b] and couple of other furnishings. Now the mellow blues and serenity of the abandoned shrine is punctuated with mischievous flicker of orange flames.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/IwjPT7E.gif[/img]

But not only that, [b]Wing’s Rest also received a slight lighting improvements for the base version as well[/b]. Speaking of, this update brings some more improvements and fixes.
[h2]Patch Notes[/h2] 
[list] 
[*] Wand projectiles change colors according to element.
[*] Light Reveal is more helpful.
[*] Fixed Useable Items equipping wrong slot when used.
[*] Fixed Critical hit effect position.
[*] Fixed Garrat not moving without reloading.
[*] Fixed menu bugs.
[*] Tried to fix projectile accuracy.
[*] Slightly improved lighting in Wing’s Rest.
[*] Fixed Backwards Khopesh.
[*] Added Halloween items.
[*] Added more character portraits.
[*] Made the main menu look better.
[/list]
[h2]Lunar Divination[/h2]
We’d like to give a brief update on [b]the new languages and Steam Trading cards[/b] we teased in June of this year.

First of all — [b]localization process is its finale phase, the in-game testing.[/b] Since Lunacid features quite a bit of text written in a lot of different formats (item and spell descriptions, menus, dialogues, notes) we need to make sure that everything looks similar to the baseline English version in terms of visual presentation and clarity. It might take a bit more time, but don’t worry — the localization update is [b]closer than you think.[/b]

As for the [b]Steam Trading cards — these are almost ready[/b], actually! Hopefully we can release them [b]this month[/b], if everything gets approved by Valve. Don’t forget to check out the full-sized card arts when they drop, as they’re not simply “small art now big”. 

[b]Once again, thank you so much for all your support and love. And remember, the Moon has its phases, and the story of Lunacid isn’t quite over just yet.[/b]

Moonlight watch thee.

notes.content:
Greetings!
It’s been some time since our last update, but just like the Moon we rise up again. 

First of all, [b]Lunacid is currently on sale with a -15% off deal[/b] — the discount will run for 14 days, so don’t miss a chance to get your hands on the game.

[previewyoutube=8rzFXKtQFGQ;full]https://youtu.be/8rzFXKtQFGQ[/previewyoutube]

Next, [b]we actually have a publisher now — Critical Reflex![/b] Thanks to their support the [b]game is about to get extended localization support.[/b] Together we can finally [b]make the game more accessible and immersive for everyone,[/b] no matter what language you may speak. 

First batch of translations will include:
[list]
[*] Brazilian Portuguese
[*] Chinese (Simplified)
[*] Polish
[*] Russian

This is [b]not the whole list of translations[/b] that are planned, but [b]these languages will be [b]integrated into the game in the upcoming weeks.[/b] If your language of preference is missing — let us know in the comments! 

Another upcoming addition alongside the localization is [b]finally getting Steam Trading Cards.[/b] All of your favorite characters are getting their new portraits, so here’s a small teaser.

notes.title: Even beyond the smash hits, 2023 was one of the best years ever for RPGs
notes.content:
Between Baldur's Gate 3's reception deservedly snowballing into an award-sweeping phenomenon and Phantom Liberty bringing a fresh dose of sci-fi spying to Cyberpunk 2077, one of the oldest and often the very nerdiest gaming genres has had a truly impressive year. Whether your personal preference leans more towards swords and sorcery or hot hacking action, both games somehow make marrying immersive narratives with tech-pushing graphical splendour look easy. Either one could easily devour every last minute of someone's free time all by themselves…

Which is a bit of a problem, as even away from the triple-A spotlight RPGs have been having one of their best years ever.

2023 has seen the genre generously throw out delicious stat-filled treats in every obscure niche, while reminding us that great RPGs don't necessarily need to be industrial strength budget-busting attention hoovers to be worth dedicating our evenings and weekends to. There just aren't enough hours in the day to play them all.

It's odd that one of the big publishers of not-so-big RPGs this year was Square Enix, a company that's long made a habit of throwing Bahamut-sized bags of money at its flagship RPGs. Although us PC gamers may still be twiddling our thumbs and wondering where the heck Final Fantasy 16 is, the Japanese publisher has still given us a great range of smaller—but definitely not lesser—games to keep ourselves busy with. This year's selection actually reminded me of its unstoppable PlayStation days, back when for every chart-topping Final Fantasy there seemed to be something a little more unusual and interesting launching at the same time.

Between Octopath Traveller 2, Star Ocean Second Story R, and Live A Live, we've gotten three different modern takes on roleplaying's past, the first trying to bring an idealised slice of the '90s into the 21st century and the latter two bringing actual '90s games up to 2023 standards. They're all delivered via charming pixel art / 3D hybrid styles that evoke the days of battery saves and chunky cartridges without forgetting that those days happened almost three decades ago (I'm sorry for scaring you like that, fellow millennials)... Read more.

notes.title: Addressing some complaints
notes.content:
Hi addressing some complaints here. Version 1.0 added pronouns to character creation in Lunacid, which some people are upset about because they exist, and some people are upset because they think it’s a cheap tactic to make people mad, and that I’m hurting people who normally use them.

Originally yes, I did add them as a spiteful response to a similar drama about Starfield. Earlier than that when I noticed them in Baulder’s Gate 3 I was happy that I could be my NB self, and thought wow I really should have added them in my Character Creator. I’ve had similar ideas about adding a gender slider in the past. But that idea didn’t really have a purpose in my eyes until I got mad that day.

Some people who are quoting my tweet have also been leaving out my second one, where I clarified a bit because I thought it could be interpreted badly. I said this under my “I’m adding em, Just to make people mad”,

[b]In a fantasy world you should be able to be whatever you want.[/b]

I do think it helps roleplaying a bit, even though there’s no place they are used in-game. I tried to think of some scenarios when they would be used, but talking about the player in third person only happens once in the game, and it’s after the final boss anyway.

Games should be a safe place, where we can experience a world we cannot in real life. And while pronouns are more and more commonplace in real life, where I live in NC, they are not. Which gives me more of a reaction than some to outrages over this small thing.

I wanted to use my control over my world, but I understand that Lunacid isn’t just mine. It belongs to all of you. If you don’t like pronouns existing at all, you are going to have a tougher and tougher time coping as the world progresses without you. And if I hurt you because you feel that I weaponized your differences or your pain, then I am very sorry.

 I want this game to be uplifting, I want it to be a dream in which you can experience triumph over impossible odds and then wake up at the end and bring newfound confidence with you. In reality I am just emulating the dreams I had when I was near ending my life. They became lucid and when I triumphed in them and woke up, I brought those feelings with me, and they helped me. That’s what this game is about, and if I’m doing the opposite then I’m not a very good game designer.

notes.title: Early Access is Out!
notes.content:
[b]Lunacid is officially out in Early Access![/b]

For $6.99 you can get the game early and play it right now! Currently it’s got 6 huge levels to explore and secrets to find, with more on the way.

And If you’d like to wait until the full release, that’s great too! Please wishlist the game and I’ll make more of a rukus when it’s done!
